evidence: Breiding et al. supply Minkowski/wedge-product formulations for expected determinants, including dependent columns grouped into independent blocks; they do not evaluate covariance between two overlapping absolute determinants with shared random unit vectors, or sum their overlaps across every triple, nor derive the non-Gaussian spherical-harmonic limit.

Schneider supplies expected valuations and a first-order U-statistic central limit theorem when the first projection variance is positive. Here that variance is zero for unit Haar-spherical vectors; the article does not give an alternative second-order spectral limit or the two-index covariance constant.

Kabluchko–Zaporozhets give expected Gaussian zonotope volume via Gaussian orthogonal projections; their generators have nonconstant radial norms and their result concerns first moments. Even after using the Gaussian angular/radial factorization, their mean formula alone does not imply the present second moments or degenerate second-order limit.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Means cannot imply second moments. The positive-first-projection CLT cannot imply the non-Gaussian second projection limit. A second-moment formula for a single Haar projection of an orthotope does not cover iid sums of randomly oriented 3D segments. General U-statistic theory could be specialized after deriving a new kernel spectrum, but does not directly entail the evaluated claim.
